overview.description: The western blot (immunoblot) separates proteins by size, transfers them to a membrane, and detects your target with antibodies. It's the standard for confirming a specific protein's identity and relative abundance.
objectives: block and probe with primary/secondary antibodies

steps.description: The western blot (immunoblot) separates proteins by size, transfers them to a membrane, and detects your target with antibodies. It's the standard for confirming a specific protein's identity and relative abundance.
steps.intro: The western blot (immunoblot) separates proteins by size, transfers them to a membrane, and detects your target with antibodies. It's the standard for confirming a specific protein's identity and relative abundance.

instructions.title: Run & transfer
instructions.description: Run an SDS-PAGE gel, then transfer the proteins to a membrane (wet or semi-dry).

instructions.title: Block
instructions.description: Block the membrane to prevent non-specific antibody binding.

instructions.title: Probe
instructions.description: Incubate with a primary antibody, wash, then a labelled secondary antibody.

instructions.title: Detect
instructions.description: Develop with chemiluminescent or fluorescent detection and image the blot.

submission.description: Submit a western blot image showing a specific band for your target, with the ladder for size reference.
